Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 100, verse 1:

﴿By the racers﴾: the horses that run in battle and snort, ﴿snorting﴾: it is the sound from their bellies when they run.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 100, verse 2:

﴿By those that strike sparks of fire﴾: the horses, which strike fire ﴿by striking [the stones]﴾ with their hooves when they travel over stony ground at night.
﴿Then by those that raid at dawn﴾ — the horses raid the enemy at the time of dawn, with their riders making the raid.
﴿Then they stir up﴾ [they agitate] ﴿thereby﴾ [at the place of their charge, or at that time] ﴿dust﴾ [dust], by the intensity of their movement.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 100, verse 5:

﴿Then they burst into the midst of the gathering﴾ with the dust (bi-l-naq') ﴿in a body﴾ from the running; i.e., they came into its midst. The verb is conjoined to the noun (ism) because the noun is in the sense of a verb; i.e., "and those who ran, then struck sparks, then made raids at dawn."
﴿Indeed, mankind﴾, the disbeliever, ﴿is ungrateful to his Lord﴾, ungrateful, denying His blessing, may He be exalted.

And indeed he is, concerning that, a witness (﴿وإنَّهُ عَلى ذَلِكَ﴾) — that is, to his ingratitude (ﷲ ... ) — ﴿لَشَهِيد﴾, bearing witness against himself by his own deeds.

Note on the translation: the Arabic term "كَنُود" (kanud, "ungrateful") is glossed here as "ingratitude," and the Qur'anic text is rendered as: "And indeed he is, concerning that, a witness" and "indeed he is a witness" for ﴿لَشَهِيد﴾.

And indeed he is, out of love of wealth, ﴿truly intense﴾ in his love for it, so he withholds it.

Wait, let me give the faithful translation as requested:

And indeed he, in his love of good (i.e., wealth), is truly intense in his love for it, so he is stingy with it.
﴿Does he not know that when what is in the graves is scattered﴾ means it is stirred up and brought out, ﴿what is in the graves﴾ of the dead, i.e., they are raised up.
﴿Wa-hussila﴾ means it was made manifest and separated out, ﴿ma fi as-sudur﴾ (what is in the breasts), meaning the hearts, of disbelief and faith.

Qur'anic verse: ﴿Indeed, their Lord, about them, on that Day, is All-Aware.﴾

Commentary: "Lakhabir" means: He is knowing (la'alim), so He will recompense them for their disbelief. The pronoun was made plural (u'ida al-damir jam'an) in consideration of the meaning of "al-insan" (mankind). This sentence indicates the object of "ya'lam" (to know), meaning: We will recompense him at the time he mentioned. "Khabir" is connected to "yawma'idh" (on that Day), and He, exalted is He, is All-Aware always, because it is the Day of Recompense.
